features.description: Self-hosted AI assistant ('the AI that really does things') whose state, memory, and credentials live on your own hardware; stewarded by the OpenClaw Foundation (501(c)(3)) with no paid tier, hosted service, or token.

One long-lived Gateway process per host is the local control plane for sessions, tools, events, and every channel connection; it exposes a typed WebSocket API (JSON-schema-validated frames, server-push events like agent, chat, presence, health, heartbeat, cron) on default 127.0.0.1:18789.
Install via curl script (macOS/Linux/WSL2), PowerShell script (Windows), or npx openclaw@latest; requires Node 24.x/26.x (Bun is an explicit opt-in runtime).
Run the always-on Gateway on a VPS or cloud host: Azure, Daytona, EasyRunner, exe.dev, Fly.io, GCP, and Hetzner (Docker), plus a VPS hosting hub and container install paths.
Installs as a LaunchAgent (macOS), systemd user service (Linux/WSL2), or Scheduled Task (Windows) so the agent runs 24/7 and survives reboots; gateway start waits for health and readiness checks.
Guided onboarding reuses a detected Claude Code or Codex CLI login or API key (Quick start) or walks a full Custom setup; reopenable via openclaw configure or openclaw onboard --classic.
Reach the Gateway from anywhere via Tailscale/VPN (recommended) or an SSH tunnel; TLS with optional pinning is available for remote WebSocket setups.

Companion devices (macOS, iOS, watchOS, Android, headless) pair to the Gateway as nodes and expose device commands — camera capture, screen recording, location, SMS (Android), notifications, and system info — via node.invoke.
Native apps for macOS (menu bar app), Windows (Windows Hub, with a cross-platform Tauri backup), iOS, Android, and a Linux desktop companion; the core is TypeScript on Node.
Multiple isolated OpenClaw instances on one machine via OPENCLAW_PROFILE: separate state directories (~/.openclaw-<profile>), workspaces, and per-profile services.
The same product runs as a personal claw (one person's assistant) or a multiplayer claw (one Gateway shared by a team) — multiplayer is configuration, not a separate edition.

Each agent's home directory (default ~/.openclaw/workspace) holds instructions, persona, memory, and skills as plain Markdown you can read, edit, and back up; editable via Settings → Agents → Files in the Control UI; separate from ~/.openclaw, which stores config and credentials.

Operating instructions and memory policy loaded at the start of every session; the place for rules, priorities, and how-to-behave details, with a default template and a '## Tools' section for local tool conventions.
Persona, tone, and boundaries loaded every session, with a dedicated personality guide and template in the docs.
The agent's name, vibe, and emoji, created or updated during the first-run bootstrap ritual.
Optional directive-based user profile — stable preferences, communication style, relationships, active projects — injected each session with a dedicated 4,000-character budget.

On a brand-new workspace the agent runs a one-time bootstrap that seeds AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, IDENTITY.md, USER.md and walks the agent through picking an identity; BOOTSTRAP.md is deleted once the workspace looks configured.
Optional startup checklist executed on Gateway startup via the bundled boot-md hook.
Keep the workspace and its memory files in a private Git repository; docs cover init, copying per-agent session databases, and moving a workspace to a new machine without rerunning onboarding.

Permanent operating authority for defined programs, kept in workspace files (typically AGENTS.md) and injected into every session automatically; combinable with automations for time-based enforcement.

The same agent is reachable on 33 documented channels — WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, Slack, Signal, iMessage, Google Chat, Microsoft Teams, Matrix, IRC, LINE, Feishu, Mattermost, Nextcloud Talk, Nostr, QQ, Twitch, WeChat, WeCom, Zalo, and more; channels run simultaneously and route per chat.
Official plugin with QR pairing over a Baileys session, install-on-demand; exactly one WhatsApp session per Gateway host, with access controls and delivery operations.
Bundled grammY bot-token channel; the fastest to set up (openclaw channels add --channel telegram).
Native iMessage support via imsg (JSON-RPC over stdio) with replies, tapbacks, effects, polls, attachments, and group management.
Bundled plugin for mentions, allowlisted public replies, thread context, and event modes.
Twilio SMS/MMS with webhooks, access controls, and delivery status.
Connect external agents to OpenClaw through the A2A 1.0 JSON-RPC protocol (bundled plugin).
Guarded, end-to-end-encrypted messaging between OpenClaw agents run by different people (bundled plugin).
Per-channel group policy: allowlists, mention gating, and isolated group sessions; Slack MPIMs route as group chats.
Discord, LINE, Matrix, Slack, and Telegram bots post one grounded, toolless, 60-second-bounded introduction when joining an allowed group — once per room with a 90-day durable claim.
Supported always-on rooms feed unmentioned chatter to the agent as quiet context without triggering replies.
Shared protection on bot-authored inbound channels stops bot pairs from replying to each other indefinitely.
Unknown DM senders get a pairing code instead of being processed; per-channel allowFrom lists and mention gates control who can message the agent.

Voice Call plugin adds phone calls via Plivo, Telnyx, or Twilio: outbound notifications, inbound calls with allowlist policy and per-number routing, full-duplex realtime voice, streaming transcription, and TTS with an ElevenLabs override.
Google Meet calls, including Twilio sessions delegated through Voice Call.
Every inbound message routes to a session owned by the Gateway: DMs share one rolling main session by default, while groups, rooms, cron runs, and webhooks get isolated sessions.
/new and /reset (configurable resetTriggers) start a fresh session with daily/idle reset policies; /btw and /side stay ephemeral.
Long conversations are summarized (compaction, /compact) and tool results trimmed (session pruning) so prompts stay lean in 24/7 chats.
Full-text recall across past transcripts.

Memory is plain Markdown with no hidden state: MEMORY.md (curated long-term facts and decisions), memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md daily notes, and an optional DREAMS.md dream diary; useful material from daily notes is distilled into MEMORY.md over time.
Daily memory files are indexed so the agent can recall past notes via the memory_search and memory_get tools without injecting everything into every prompt.
Files recorded as untrusted, or written remotely without valid provenance, are excluded from automatic memory context; openclaw doctor lists each excluded MEMORY.md or USER.md.
Continue the same Gateway-owned session from the Control UI, the terminal, or a coding harness (session synchronization and attachment).
Interactive sessions generate a topic title in the background when the first message is dispatched.
Sessions can be published as revocable public links with an anonymous read-only view and content exclusions (shipped in v2026.10.5).

features.feature: Personal user files on a shared Gateway
features.description: On multi-user Gateways each authenticated requester keeps a personal USER.md, read and updated through the Gateway via the personal_instructions tool.

Markdown instruction packs (YAML frontmatter plus body) that teach the agent repeatable workflows, loaded with documented precedence from workspace, project, personal, managed, workshop, bundled, and plugin sources.
Skill visibility scopes by path: per-agent workspace skills, project-agent skills, personal ~/.agents/skills, shared managed skills, workshop skills, and extra dirs.
Agents learn and save their own skills with change history and undo; Skill Workshop 2.0 shipped in v2026.10.5.
Turn past conversations into reusable skills through a steerable chat (introduced in v2026.9.4).
Step-by-step guide and templates for authoring custom skills, whose slash commands register automatically.

Packages that add tools, skills, channels, model providers, speech, realtime voice, media generation, web search/fetch, and hooks; installed from ClawHub, npm, git, local dirs, or archives and applied to a running Gateway.
Typed SDK for building plugins, including agent-harness plugins that replace the embedded agent executor and in-process tool/prompt/message hooks.
Agents can inspect, install, enable, disable, remove, and reload plugins from an conversation.

Public marketplace (clawhub.ai) for community skills and plugins: search/install/update via the openclaw CLI, publish via the clawhub CLI; semver versions, changelogs, download counts, stars, and security scan summaries on public pages.
A connected node publishes skills installed in its own ~/.openclaw/skills; they appear in the agent skill list while the node is connected and execute with exec host=node.
On a shared Gateway, identified operators create and import personal skills (Plugins → Skills) without permission to change shared workspace skills or Gateway config.

Typed tool categories: runtime (exec, process, terminal, code_execution), files (read, write, edit, apply_patch), human input (ask_user, secrets), web (web_search, x_search, web_fetch), browser, messaging, sessions/agents, automation, gateway/nodes, plugin lifecycle, and media.

Run shell commands in the workspace — foreground, background, or durable across Gateway restarts — on the Gateway host, in a sandbox, or on a paired node, with an automatic host memory budget on Linux.
Built-in web_search, x_search (X posts), and web_fetch (readable page content) tools.

Agent-driven dedicated Chromium-family profile (Chrome/Brave/Edge) isolated from your personal browser: tab control, click/type/drag/select, snapshots, screenshots, PDFs, page-text Q&A, and downloads, bounded by an SSRF policy; a user profile attaches to your signed-in Chrome via Chrome DevTools MCP.
Offload browsing to Browserless (hosted or Docker), Browserbase, Notte, direct WebSocket CDP providers, or the zero-config node browser proxy.
Sign a browser profile into a site once, before the agent automates it.
The agent pauses and asks the human a structured question; choices surface as answer cards in chat and the native apps.
Agents obtain a credential from the user without ever seeing its value.
Fine-grained tool allow/deny by profile, agent, provider, channel, and sandbox state — with per-agent restrictions for delegated runs — testable via openclaw policy.

Optional sandbox backends — Docker (default), Podman, SSH, OpenShell, and Crabbox cloud boxes — isolate tool execution and the browser from the host, with per-session sandbox workspaces; off by default.
Explicit, per-message escape hatch (/exec, tools.elevated) for authorized senders to run a command outside the sandbox.
Compact JavaScript programs that combine many tools in one call against a hidden OpenClaw tool catalog, without sending every tool schema to the model.
tool_search / tool_describe / dispatch_action let the agent search, inspect, and call large tool catalogs without prompt bloat.
Durable progress cards update the parent session on long-running work (unavailable to sub-agents).
get_goal, create_goal, and update_goal tools maintain durable goals for the agent.
Read-only diff viewer and file renderer for agents.

Chat command surface: standalone commands (/new, /status), session directives (/think, /fast, /verbose, /model, /queue, /elevated), inline shortcuts (/help), and host-only bang (!) bash commands for authorized senders.
Agents can arrange Control UI panes (screen) and create appearance themes (theme) from chat.

Connect Model Context Protocol servers (stdio command or streamable-http URL) via openclaw mcp add or Settings; exposed tools pass through the same tool policy as built-in tools, with per-server include filters.
openclaw mcp serve exposes Gateway-backed channel conversations to external MCP clients such as Claude Code over stdio.
Paired nodes publish MCP tools and local model inference to Gateway agents.
MCP server events trigger Automation runs through subscribed, signed callbacks.

features.feature: MCP Apps in the Control UI
features.description: MCP App discovery and management surface in the web UI (introduced in v2026.10.1).

Built-in scheduler for one-shot reminders (--at), recurring intervals, and cron expressions — each job with its own context, delivery policy, quiet hours (activeHours), idleOnly, and run history, editable by both user and agent.
Authenticated HTTP ingress lets external services start agent runs.

Event-driven HOOK.md scripts react to lifecycle events (session /new, /reset, /stop, compaction, gateway startup, message flow), managed with openclaw hooks; plugin hooks intercept tool calls in-process.
Periodic proactive wake-ups; legacy heartbeat monitors migrate into ordinary editable automation jobs with their own execution policies.
Sender-gated inbound email triggers isolated reader sessions.
Runs local pipelines with resumable approvals.

Background agent runs spawned from a parent run, each in its own session with isolated tool policy by default, configurable nesting depth, and results announced back to the requester; visible and steerable in the Control UI Subagents panel.
Structured fan-out and collection of concurrent worker agents, orchestrated from Code Mode.
Delegate turns to external coding harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) through Agent Client Protocol sessions, including thread-bound and resumable runs.
Agents send messages across conversations, channels, and to other agents; cross-provider messaging can be restricted.
Redirect a running agent mid-task; queue or steer follow-ups from chat and the native apps.

Run multiple isolated agents in one Gateway — each with its own workspace, state directory, model registry, and SQLite session store — with bindings routing channel accounts (e.g., two WhatsApp numbers) to the right agent.
Give a job its own agent and package it as a Template to share with others.
Set up teams of specialist agents (v2026.9.5) and role-scoped parallel specialist lanes for a single job.

One Gateway shared by a whole team: shared sessions everyone can open and steer in the Control UI, live presence, named operator roles, verified GitHub identity with commit credit, and a production deployment path with Cloudflare Access or Tailscale identity sign-in.
Ownership, participants, owner assignment, and DM session isolation for multiple people on one Gateway.
Repository tasks run in managed Git branch/checkouts; publish PRs from a selected GitHub account and follow CI results in the conversation.

Bring your own keys or subscriptions: OpenAI (API or ChatGPT/Codex OAuth), Anthropic, Google Gemini/Vertex, Z.AI GLM, OpenRouter, Kilo Gateway, Vercel AI Gateway, MiniMax, NVIDIA, xAI, Moonshot Kimi, Volcano Engine/BytePlus, and more — with multi-key rotation and defined key priority.
Run models locally via llama.cpp, LM Studio, Ollama, vLLM, SGLang, or local proxies such as LiteLLM through custom base URLs.

A self-updating model catalog merges models.dev data with OpenClaw manifests and price feeds, publishing every four hours to catalog.openclaw.ai; running Gateways pick up new models without an update or restart.
Primary plus fallback chains, model aliases, modelPolicy allowlists, auth-profile rotation inside a provider before failing over, and dedicated utility, image, PDF, and decision model slots.
openclaw models lists, sets, scans, aliases, fallbacks, and authenticates providers (paste-api-key, OAuth login, subscription setup).
Use an existing ChatGPT subscription as model access via OAuth (Beta, v2026.9.7).
Swap the agent loop itself: embedded OpenClaw runtime, Codex, or the GitHub Copilot agent runtime (always explicit opt-in); models and harnesses are plugins.
Usage tracking, prompt-caching controls (cacheRetention), Anthropic 1M-context sizing, image dimension caps, and /compact guidance for reducing token pressure.
Live voice conversation on a node with three modes: provider-native realtime, streaming stt-tts, and observe-only transcription.
Wake-word capture on a node hands the conversation to the agent.
Inbound voice notes are transcribed via batch STT providers (Deepgram, ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Google, xAI, and more); replies can be spoken aloud via the synchronous tts tool.

image_generate, video_generate, and music_generate run as async background jobs across 25+ providers (OpenAI, Google, fal, ComfyUI, Runway, PixVerse, MiniMax, and more) and post results to the chat when ready.
Vision-capable providers summarize inbound images, audio, and video, including node-captured photos, clips, and screen recordings.
Assistant audio and video play inline across the Control UI and native apps.

Official App Store app (iOS/iPadOS 26.2+): Gateway chat over LAN or tailnet, node capabilities (screen snapshot, camera, location, Talk mode, voice wake, opt-in Health summaries), read-only workspace browsing, an offline transcript cache, and a durable outbox queueing messages sent while offline.
Official Google Play (and signed APK) companion-node app: chat, attention indicators for pending questions and approvals, thread snooze, an automations view, and a Gateway settings assistant.
Menu bar app that connects as a node, adding widget-panel (Canvas), camera, screen, notification, and computer-control commands, plus an Instances device UI.
Native Windows Hub desktop app (recommended), a cross-platform Tauri app as backup, a PowerShell install for terminal-first use, or WSL2 for the most Linux-compatible runtime.
Desktop control on a paired node (gated), letting the agent operate a real GUI.
OpenClaw worker sessions can be hosted on devices with placement, capacity limits, and container isolation.
Codex, Claude, OpenCode, and Pi sessions and transcripts are discovered on the Gateway and paired nodes.
Terminal uploads plus a File Transfer plugin for directory listing, fetch, and write between the Gateway host and paired nodes.
A docs hub for connecting, pairing, and securing devices across localhost, LAN, and tailnet — one Gateway owns all state, so every chat surface and app sees the same sessions.

Gateway-served web app on port 18789: chat and sessions, Settings (models and providers, devices, agents and files, plugins, MCP, appearance themes, language), usage, activity recaps, a meetings page, agent-memory import, and built-in bug-report links; custom UI builds can be mounted.
Terminal user interface via the openclaw command.
Browser-based chat over the Gateway WebSocket (included in core).
Persistent widget boards attached to a session — hosted widget documents with defined sandbox and capability boundaries, presentable natively on the macOS widget panel.
Agents render Mermaid diagrams across chat surfaces (v2026.9.1).

Conservative defaults (loopback bind, DM pairing codes, group allowlists with mention gates) plus openclaw security audit with a severity catalog and auto-fixes, hardened baseline configs, prompt-injection guidance, browser/SSRF risk docs, a secrets storage map, rate limiting, and incident-response runbooks.
Adversarial threats to the OpenClaw platform and ClawHub mapped to MITRE ATLAS.
Every WebSocket client and node presents a device identity; new device IDs require pairing approval and receive device tokens; connect frames are challenge-signed and pinned to paired metadata.

Shared-secret token or password, Tailscale Serve identity, trusted-proxy operator identity (e.g., Cloudflare Access), or none for private ingress; gateway.auth applies to all connections, local or remote.
Named operator roles and connection scopes bound what each person can do on a shared Gateway.
By default OpenClaw phones home for nothing but a daily version check; anonymous feature statistics are opt-in, and update.checkOnStart: false disables both.
Full CLI surface: gateway install/start/status, configure, channels add, models, skills, plugins, mcp, nodes, hooks, sessions, memory, security, policy, automations, infer, and docs search.
openclaw doctor runs read-only health checks with fixes; openclaw triage turns a broken install into a sanitized diagnosis prompt handed to Claude Code, Codex CLI, or the built-in OpenClaw agent.
Config and plugin changes apply to the running Gateway without a restart by default.
Backup archives, per-database snapshots, scheduling, and offsite copies of state and workspace, plus update rollback and recovery safeguards.
Official support routes and community forums (community.openclaw.ai), plus private security reporting channels.
